title.narrative: Scaling Up Nutrition Learning and Evaluation (SUN L&E)

description.narrative: (Zambia): Zambia's high rates of malnutrition-based child stunting have persisted for several decades at up to 45-50 percent in rural areas. According to Zambia's Demographic and Health Survey 2018, nation-wide stunting levels reduced to 35 from 40 percent in 2014 at the national level, but more can be done to reduce this. The Scaling Up Nutrition Learning and Evaluation (SUN LE) mechanism contributes to the Government of the Republic of Zambia (GRZ)-led 1,000 Most Critical Days Program (MCDP) that aims to reduce stunting through interventions to address malnutrition in partnership with a coalition of donors. SUN LE is the learning and evaluation arm of the entire MCDP, including USAID's Scaling Up Nutrition Technical Assistance mechanism. This includes identifying, designing, and testing solutions to more effectively understand and measure outcomes to attain the GRZ and donors' joint goal of reducing stunting. Fiscal Year 2022 funds will be used to conduct a performance assessment and focused studies on the implementation of GRZ nutrition services to promote learning around stunting issues, to inform the greater GRZ and multi-donor supported MCDP and support the upgrade of the National Food and Nutrition Commission website to allow the posting of the nutrition research and communications products. SUN LE will be collecting and disseminating data to identify and promote development breakthroughs around stunting and use the data to modify and improve activities. This mechanism prevents stunting in future generations and supports USAID's Development Objective 3: Capacity of Zambia's Government, Citizens and Private Sector Increased to Improve Health Outcomes and Meet Critical Needs of Vulnerable Populations. This mechanism contributes directly to the Administration priority of building global health security capacity by investing in basic health care systems..
